Desk Buddy · covered-shell design · preview version 7.2 · tuft pointing down · 1 Oct 2026

One face, not two.

The screen draws his nose and mouth, so the physical muzzle is gone. What still says dog with the screen dark: the ears, Spike’s forehead tuft, the brow and cheek line, the collar and the tag. The camera hides at the root of the tuft, and the collar tag carries the Mix 1 logo. Try the Tuft, Tag and Screen buttons, and the colours at the bottom left.

New in version 7

One face decided 1 Oct

  • No physical muzzle. The screen draws the nose and mouth, so there is only one face.
  • A slightly raised face plate frames the screen. Its top edge makes two soft brows with a small dip between them, and its lower corners round out into full cheeks.
  • Switched off, the dog read comes from the ears, the brow and cheek line, the collar and the tag.

Forehead tuft pointing down in 7.2

  • New in 7.2: the tuft can hang down, like a little fringe from just under the top edge of the head, with the tips drooping down and slightly forward. The camera peeks out from under the tips. Tuft direction flips between Down (default) and the 7.1 Up tuft.
  • A little puppy hair lick, centred above the screen: four or five short, rounded locks that grow from one soft base, all turn the same way and sweep back over the head. Pointing up, it is about half the height of the v7 tuft, so it never competes with the ears.
  • Two shapes with the Tuft shape buttons: Plush (default: chunkier, rounder tips) and Flick (five slimmer locks, a livelier flame).
  • The base is wide and thin, so it grows out of the forehead instead of sitting on it.
  • Colour runs from the head's cream at the roots to caramel tips, like a fur highlight. Chocolate runs cream into chocolate tips.
  • Pointing up, the camera sits in a small notch under the front edge of the tuft. Pointing down, it sits just under the drooping tips. Either way it looks straight ahead. The measured clear cone past the fur is shown under the picture (always at least 70 degrees).
  • The ears are plain. Inner ear shows an optional soft darker-caramel triangle.

Logo tag decorative

  • The gold bone is gone. A satin-steel tag with a glossy enamel face carries the Mix 1 logo.
  • Three shapes to compare: a rounded square (the logo's own shape), a round coin and an enamel pill with the name.
  • It hangs from a small steel slide on the collar and stops above the chest obstacle sensor, so it never blocks it.

What changed in the covered shell (v2)

Legs like Petoi Bittle, Sony aibo

  • Each flat leg plate becomes a two-piece shell: a white outer half and a dark inner cover.
  • The knee servo sits inside the thigh. The wheel servo sits inside a paw pod at the bottom of the shin.
  • Every joint is a round knuckle with an even 0.8 mm gap, so it looks the same at any angle.
  • Servo arms are buried inside the next piece. Each output gets one snap-in hub cap, 13 in total.

Wires like Unitree Go2

  • Leads run inside each leg in a covered channel.
  • At the knee and the hip they wrap half a turn around the joint inside a closed round chamber, so they never pull tight or poke out.
  • They enter the body through a slot hidden behind the hip cup. The four open belly slots are gone.

Body

  • Dark side panels cover the hip servo mounts. The round hip cups sit on them like shoulders.
  • Snap-in dark bands on the chest and rump hide the lid screws and frame the obstacle sensors.
  • The tail servo moves under the lid. The tail sits on a round turntable, and you only see the cap.
  • A dark collar fills the open gap between the head and the body.

Head and face

  • The camera and gesture windows become a matching pair, one each side of centre.
  • The muzzle's open back is closed by the collar.
  • The side screws move underneath. The USB-C holes get flush snap-in doors, one each side so it looks balanced.
  • The speaker grille is centred on the back. The BOOT and RESET pinholes are removed.
  • The ears are tapered, lean back, and are keyed with a hidden screw, so they come off instead of snapping off.

Switch, battery, ports

  • The power rocker moves to the front of the belly, flush in a recess.
  • A new belly door holds the battery, so the lid never comes off to reach it.
  • The charge port becomes a neat pill-shaped opening in the rump band, sized to the plug.

Surface

  • Rounded edges everywhere: 3 to 12 mm depending on the part. That includes an 8 mm round under the chest and rump, which the knee pods need to swing past.
  • Seams sit on colour breaks, never across a smooth face.
  • Two colours plus one accent. Warm white on top, graphite below and on the inner leg covers.
  • Light raised ovals show where to touch.

What it costs

A bit wider and heavier

Lower body 84 → 97 mm, about 95 g more. The wheels still set the overall width at 170 mm.

Legs still look layered

Each joint still steps out about 11 mm, and you can see the dark knee and paw pods from the front. A slim leg needs the knee servo moved into the body, a much bigger redesign.

More printing, harder assembly

About 45 printed pieces instead of 24, plus snap fits and 13 caps. Test coupons for the knee, hip and snaps come first.

Heat

Closed pods trap servo heat. I'll put a thermometer in one after 10 minutes of walking. Above 45 °C, those parts get printed in PETG.

Wire wear

Each leg's leads flex at two joints. Stock servo wire may fatigue over months. Silicone wire is the fix if it does.

Two small layout flips

The knee servos turn to point outward, and all four paws face forward. That's only a horn calibration change, and it stops the covers from hitting the belly.

Decided on 26 Sep

Build approach

chosenEvery servo stays where it is, and each leg is wrapped in a two-piece shell. Moving the knee servos into the body with push-rods stays an idea for a later version.

Colours

chosenWarm white on top, graphite below and on the inner leg covers. The 13 hub caps and other small covers are black. The eyes are white; they're drawn by software, so their colour can change any time.

Wheels

chosenProper wheels with a black hub cap, the way Loona does it. No paw hood.

Wider lower body

chosenThe side panels make the lower body 97 mm wide instead of 84.

Power switch

chosenA flush rocker at the front of the belly.

Battery door

chosenA screwed door on the belly carries the battery holder, so the lid never comes off for the battery.

Bigger tyres

chosen26 mm × 2.4 mm O-rings, so the paw pods clear the desk by about 4 mm.

I'll handle these in the build

  • Measure four servo sizes on the real MG90S when the parts arrive. The shells use estimates until then, and the fit coupon checks them.
  • Move the charge port up into the rump band, so it clears the rounded bottom edge.
  • Add rounding and shell tools to my SolidWorks script. Right now it can only make boxes, cylinders and flat outlines.
  • Re-run the clash check, the balance check and the file checks on the covered model, and show you the real SolidWorks pictures.
